Cc: ClearHealth Procurement <procurement@clearhealth.com>

Subject: Follow-up on today's demo — request for feature-level econ

Thanks for the demo this morning — great clarity on latency and routing. As we discussed, the execs at ClearHealth want a tighter digest on the economics by feature before we push to procurement.

Specifically can you send: 1) an estimate $/1M tokens we should plan for given our mix (avg prompt+response ~1.8k tokens; 200k monthly active users with ~5 feature calls per MAU), 2) per-feature unit cost and recommended price bands, and 3) expected CAC payback for a pilot priced at $X/mo per org (we're thinking $3k/month entry for a pilot).

We need something concise for Friday's leadership readout (Jan 13). Appreciate a workbook or spreadsheet.

Emma Carter
Head of Product

emma@clearhealth.com
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up on today's demo — request for feature-level econ

Thanks Emma — good asks. Attaching a workbook that breaks down token assumptions by feature and three pricing scenarios (conservative, target, aggressive). High-level answers below; workbook has the line-by-line math.

Quick summary:
- Token volume baseline (your numbers): 200k MAU * 5 calls/mo * 1,800 tokens/call = 1.8B tokens/mo.
- Target $/1M tokens (target scenario): $1,200 per 1M tokens (this produces gross margin ~58% at our current hosted cost curve with 8-bit quantized serving).
- Per-feature unit economics (examples):
  - Smart Triage (high calls, short responses): ~0.9k tokens/call -> ~$1.08/1000 calls or ~$972 per 1M calls equivalent.
  - Summary & Notes (longer responses): ~3.2k tokens/call -> ~$3.84/1000 calls.
- CAC payback (pilot assumptions):
  - Pilot price: $3k/month. If feature drives 8 net new paying orgs in 6 months, payback per acquired org ~2.5 months. If conversion is lower (3 orgs), payback ~6.5 months. Workbook includes sensitivity table for CAC vs uplift.

Attachments: econ_workbook_v3.xlsx (includes assumptions tab, per-feature tokenization, and sensitivity). Also adding a CSV export of the feature token mapping.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) share the workbook (attached) — DONE.
2) Hands-on econ review (45m) with your product and finance — can we schedule Thu Jan 12 or Fri Jan 13?
3) If numbers look good, we'll prep a procurement-friendly pilot SOW and expected SLA/cost table.

On timing: I can join Thu 12:00–16:00 PT or Fri 08:00–12:00 PT.

--
Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up on today's demo — request for feature-level econ

Adding a couple of pricing and margin notes from a commercial standpoint.

Pricing bands (we recommend presenting these three to your execs):
- Entry pilot band: $3k/month + $1,500 per 1M tokens over 1M included (low-touch onboarding). Gross margin expectation ~45-50% in first 3 months due to onboarding/eng effort.
- Target production band: $9k/month + $1,200 per 1M tokens (recommended target for customer-facing feature set). Gross margin expectation ~55-65% after steady state.
- High-volume enterprise band: committed reserved capacity (annual) -> effective $/1M tokens can fall to $750–$900 depending on commitment and burst mix.

CAC and payback framing:
- If ClearHealth’s buyer economics assume $40k LTV per customer for the feature and CAC of $7k (sales+onsite+integration), payback at $3k/month is ~2.3 months (assuming immediate upsell to production band in month 3).
- If only 40% feature adoption within existing customers, you need to price to preserve >40% gross margin; otherwise consider chargeback per feature (metered) to maintain unit economics.

Operational note: inference cost is a fungible bucket — routing, batching, and prefix caching materially change per-token cost. We included two rows in the workbook: one using conservative per-token cost (higher) and one using optimized runtime with batching/prefix caching (lower).

I'll join the deep-dive on Thu 12:30 PT if that works.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, GTM Economics, Redwood Inference

3) Please surface your procurement contact and a sample pilot SOW template.

Scheduling: Thu 12:30 PT works for us — please send calendar invite. Procurement cc'd above — procurement@clearhealth.com — they will bring any contract redlines to the call.

Emma
